investigation.title: local-agent-runtime eval failure: upstream model provider returned 424 provider_account_unavailable, blocking all required evidence collection
investigation.summary: The local-agent-runtime observability eval failed because POST /api/agents/[REDACTED]/runtime/test returned HTTP 502, wrapping an upstream 424 Failed Dependency with error code provider_account_unavailable. Because the LLM call never completed, the probe collected zero evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message all missing), causing a total contract validation failure. This is an eval-infrastructure failure scoped to the local-agent-runtime check; sibling checks local-agent-create and local-agent-permissions both passed, confirming agent creation and permissions infrastructure are healthy.
investigation.rootCause: The AURA backend was transiently unable to reach the configured model provider at the time the eval ran (2026-10-02T12:21:10–16Z). The runtime test endpoint surfaced this as a 502 bad_gateway wrapping a 424 Failed Dependency with code provider_account_unavailable. Because the LLM response never arrived, the probe returned no evidence, and all five required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) were absent, failing the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json lines 102–105. The failure is localized to the model-provider connectivity layer for the local-agent-runtime check; no shared dependency failure is indicated by sibling results.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1769-1777: runner branch at line 1772 invokes the probe, calls requireOrgId and createAgent before issuing the runtime test; the 502 was returned from the runtime/test call, not from agent creation (which passed as a sibling).
possibleCauses: Most likely — transient model provider outage or degradation: the 424 provider_account_unavailable error with the message 'This is an issue on our side, not with your account or credits' is an explicit AURA-side signal that the provider was unreachable at eval time. This is consistent with a point-in-time provider connectivity blip.

Less likely — persistent model provider misconfiguration for the local agent type: if the local agent template is configured to use a provider or model that is currently disabled or quota-exhausted on the AURA side, the 424 would recur on every run. The single-run history (previousRunCount=0) means recurrence cannot yet be confirmed or ruled out.

investigation.title: Project Agent Chat Stream Eval Failure: Model Provider Returned 424 provider_account_unavailable, Blocking Session Persistence and Text Generation
investigation.summary: The desktop-release eval for project-agent-chat-stream failed because the AURA backend returned HTTP 424 with error code provider_account_unavailable during the chat stream turn, causing the agent to emit an error frame instead of text_delta frames. As a direct consequence, textSample remained empty and sessionId, sessionCount, and expectedPhrase were never produced, violating three required evidence assertions in the expected-output contract defined at infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 120.
investigation.rootCause: The upstream model provider was unreachable from AURA's backend at the time of the eval run (2026-10-02T12:21:21–12:21:31Z). The API returned a 424 Failed Dependency with code provider_account_unavailable and support_id 6050f83bd2ea. This terminated the chat stream before any text_delta frame, session persistence, or phrase generation could occur, causing the eval to fail its contract assertions for sessionId, sessionCount, expectedPhrase, frameTypes (missing text_delta), and textSample. This is an eval-infrastructure signal of a backend provider connectivity issue; no user-traffic or incident evidence is present in the packet to confirm a production user impact.
proof: failed-check.message: HTTP 424 with code provider_account_unavailable and support_id 6050f83bd2ea was returned during the chat stream turn.

failed-check.evidence: frameTypes observed were [progress, session_ready, assistant_message_start, error, message] — the error frame confirms the stream was terminated by the provider error before any text_delta was emitted; textSample is empty string.

expected-output.missing-required-evidence: sessionId, sessionCount, and expectedPhrase are absent from the collected evidence, matching the three assertions that require a completed, persisted chat turn.

expected-output.contract (infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 120): the contract requires frameTypes to contain text_delta and textSample to contain 'hello from aura'; neither assertion could be satisfied because the stream errored before generating text.

sibling.session-share-public-read: the session-share-public-read sibling check received the identical 424 provider_account_unavailable error (support_id 6e7c7558df96), confirming the provider outage affected at least two independent chat-stream calls within the same run window.
sibling.project-agent-tool-roundtrip: frameTypes for the tool-roundtrip sibling also contain the error frame and textSample is empty, consistent with the same provider error blocking model inference.

sibling.project-agent-a2a-roundtrip: both planner and reviewer agent streams show the error frame pattern; reviewerEventsError is 'Timed out after 120000ms waiting for expected value', consistent with the provider being unreachable.

sibling.project-agent-subagent-roundtrip: sessionSubagentError is 'Parent chat stream did not emit a child run id', and frameTypes again contain the error frame, consistent with the provider error preventing model output.

failed-check.timing: latencyMs=10707 is well below the warningLatencyMs=30000 threshold, indicating the request failed fast rather than timing out — consistent with an immediate 424 rejection from the backend.
possibleCauses: [Highest confidence] Transient model provider outage or connectivity disruption on AURA's backend side at the time of the eval run, as explicitly stated in the 424 error message: 'AURA is temporarily unable to reach the model provider. This is an issue on our side, not with your account or credits.' Both project-agent-chat-stream (support_id 6050f83bd2ea) and session-share-public-read (support_id 6e7c7558df96) received this error independently.

[Medium confidence] A provider account or routing configuration issue on AURA's backend that caused all model inference requests to be rejected with 424 during this run window, affecting all four sibling checks that depend on model inference.

investigation.title: Project Agent Tool Roundtrip Eval Failure: Model Provider Unavailable Blocks All Tool Execution (desktop-release)
investigation.summary: The project-agent-tool-roundtrip eval on desktop-release (desktop-nightly-macos-aarch64) failed because the agent stream terminated with an error frame before any tools were invoked: toolNames is empty, and writeOk, readBackOk, commandOk, and passMarkerPresent are all false. Two sibling checks (project-agent-chat-stream and session-share-public-read) surfaced an explicit HTTP 424 error with code provider_account_unavailable, strongly indicating the model provider was unreachable at eval time, which prevented the agent from generating any tool calls.
investigation.rootCause: The upstream model provider was unavailable at the time of the eval run (2026-10-02T12:21:31–12:24:35Z), causing the agent stream to emit an error frame instead of an assistant turn with tool calls. Because no tool calls were ever issued, write_file, read_file, and run_command were never invoked, and all downstream tool-roundtrip assertions failed. This is an eval-infrastructure failure caused by a transient or sustained model provider outage, not a code defect in the tool harness itself. The root cause is uncertain to the extent that it cannot be ruled out that the tool harness or agent configuration is also broken independently; the provider error is the earliest confirmed failure boundary.

sibling.project-agent-subagent-roundtrip: taskToolUsed=false, subagentSpawned=false, sessionSubagentError='Parent chat stream did not emit a child run id' — further confirms no agent turn produced tool calls during this run window.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1823-1827: runner calls runProjectToolRoundtrip via withCleanup — the runner branch was reached (check did not skip), so the failure is in the agent response, not in eval selection or token gating.
possibleCauses: Model provider outage or transient unavailability at 2026-10-02T12:21Z caused the agent to receive a 424 Failed Dependency error before generating any tool calls — supported directly by sibling checks project-agent-chat-stream and session-share-public-read (evidence ids: sibling.project-agent-chat-stream, sibling.session-share-public-read).

Agent tool harness misconfiguration or missing tool registration on the desktop-release runtime, independently preventing write_file, read_file, and run_command from being offered to the model — possible but not directly evidenced; the provider error is the earlier and more directly evidenced failure boundary.

Agent instance or project-session initialization failure that causes the stream to error before the model turn begins — consistent with the 'error' frame appearing in frameTypes and the very short latency (7804ms), but the specific error payload is not captured in the tool-roundtrip evidence (it is captured in sibling checks as the 424 provider error).

The skill was successfully created and installed on the agent (evidenced by created=true and installedOnAgent=true in failed-check.evidence, and corroborated by the passing harness-skills-roundtrip sibling), but skillInContext=false and textSample="" indicate the skill was not injected into the agent's context when the chat turn was executed. Because textSample is empty and skillLabels is an empty array, the agent either produced no usable text output or the skill context was stripped before the turn. The presence of an "error" frame type in frameTypes alongside "assistant_message_start" and "message" suggests the chat turn encountered a runtime error that may have interrupted or prevented skill context injection. No suspect changes are identified in sourceDiscovery.suspectChanges, so a regression from a specific commit cannot be asserted.

This is an eval-infrastructure failure caused by a transient or sustained model provider outage, not a code defect in the tool harness itself. Evidence that the model provider was fully healthy at 2026-10-02T12:21–12:24Z (e.g., provider status page showing no incidents) would shift the diagnosis toward an AURA-backend-internal routing or configuration failure rather than a provider-side outage.

A re-run that passes project-agent-chat-stream but still fails session-share-public-read (with a different error, not 424) would indicate a separate bug in the session share creation or public read path, independent of the provider outage.

If only the eval org/project credentials were affected (e.g., a quota or rate-limit event scoped to the eval account) and other orgs were unaffected, that would narrow the scope away from a broad provider outage.
A passing sibling check from the same run window (none exist in this packet) would disprove the hypothesis that the provider was globally unreachable for all project-agent requests.
